article.headline: Sixteen iPhone Photos, One Panorama, a Navigable 3D World
article.lede: Martin Maly, an indie developer based in Tokyo, has built a pipeline that converts sixteen iPhone photographs into a fully navigable three-dimensional world in under five minutes. By pairing his 360° photography app Teleport with World Labs' generative world model Marble, he has compressed a workflow that once required specialist hardware and hours of processing into something a single person can run from a phone. His demo — Golden Gai, the dense post-war bar district in Shinjuku — illustrates how quickly spatial AI pipelines are becoming accessible to solo builders.
article.body:
The workflow has three steps. Teleport guides the user to photograph a space from a fixed central point using the iPhone's ultra-wide lens; server-side stitching then assembles those shots into a single **equirectangular panorama** — the 2:1 rectangular format that maps a full 360° × 180° sphere onto a flat image, the same standard used by Google (GOOGL) Street View and dedicated 360° cameras. That panorama is sent to the World Labs API specifying *Marble 1.1*, their April 2026 model update. Within three to five minutes the API returns a *3D Gaussian Splat*: the scene encoded as millions of semi-transparent ellipsoids that render interactively in real time.

World Labs was founded in January 2024 by researchers with an unusual claim on the underlying technology. Ben Mildenhall co-invented *NeRF* (Neural Radiance Fields) at Google (GOOGL) Research in 2020, the volumetric approach that first made photorealistic novel-view synthesis practical. Christoph Lassner built Pulsar, an early differentiable sphere renderer that anticipated modern Gaussian Splatting. Fei-Fei Li — Stanford professor, ImageNet creator, former Google Cloud AI chief — serves as CEO. Together they have fused two generations of 3D reconstruction into a generative model that synthesizes geometry beyond the camera frame, not merely reconstructing what was photographed. The company has raised approximately $1.23 billion to date; its February 2026 round brought in NVIDIA (NVDA), AMD (AMD), and Autodesk (ADSK) as strategic investors.

The shift from NeRF to Gaussian Splatting matters for both speed and editability. A NeRF encodes a scene inside a neural network's weights and renders by casting virtual rays through a continuous volumetric field — photorealistic but slow and computationally opaque. **3D Gaussian Splatting** instead represents the scene as an explicit set of positioned, sized, and colored ellipsoids, optimized against input photographs through *differentiable rasterization*. Rendering projects those ellipsoids onto the screen directly, concentrating compute only where geometry exists. The result runs in real time on a GPU and, increasingly, in a browser — which is how World Labs delivers navigable worlds to end users.

Competitors like Luma AI and Polycam have offered Gaussian Splatting pipelines for iPhone since 2023, and Niantic Spatial's Scaniverse performs splat generation on-device without a cloud round-trip. What distinguishes World Labs' Marble is its status as a *world model* rather than a photogrammetric reconstructor: it fills in unseen angles, extends scene boundaries, and generates plausible geometry where no photograph exists. Marble 1.1 introduced "dynamic cubes," which detect when a scene needs more spatial room and add units in the same generation pass. Whether the pipeline handles Golden Gai's specific density — six alleys crammed with two-story wooden bars, exposed wiring, and hand-lettered signs stacked floor to ceiling — at acceptable fidelity is not verifiable from the demo clip alone. But the choice of location is pointed: few subjects in Tokyo compress more visual complexity into less physical space.

What Maly has demonstrated is less a product than a proof of stack. A solo developer with an existing app, no venture backing, and access to a public API assembled a 3D-world capture pipeline in what appears to be days. The integration depends entirely on World Labs having opened Marble as an API — a platform bet that echoes how Stability AI and OpenAI built developer ecosystems ahead of consumer products. As cost-per-generation falls and output fidelity rises, the applications most often cited are architectural walk-throughs, real-estate listings, heritage preservation, and location-based games.

concepts.definition: A 360° image format that maps the entire spherical field of view — 360° horizontally and 180° vertically — onto a flat rectangle with a 2:1 aspect ratio. It is the industry standard for 360° photography (used by Google Street View, Ricoh Theta, and similar systems) and is the preferred input format for World Labs' Marble API because it encodes complete spatial information about a scene. Teleport generates it by stitching multiple overlapping iPhone photos together on its servers.

A 2020 technique that encodes a 3D scene inside the weights of a neural network and renders novel viewpoints by casting virtual rays through the learned volumetric field. Co-invented by Ben Mildenhall and colleagues at Google Research, it was the first method to produce photorealistic novel-view synthesis from ordinary photographs alone, but renders slowly and is difficult to edit after training.

A scene representation introduced in 2023 that encodes a 3D space as millions of semi-transparent ellipsoids (Gaussians), each with a position, size, orientation, and color, optimized to match a set of input photographs. Unlike NeRF, the geometry is explicit and therefore editable, and rendering is fast enough to run interactively in real time. World Labs outputs scenes in a Gaussian Splat container format (.spz).

An AI system that builds an internal spatial representation of an environment and can generate or extend it beyond what was directly observed. Unlike photogrammetric reconstructors — which reproduce only what the camera captured — a world model synthesizes unseen geometry, fills in occluded surfaces, and can expand scene boundaries generatively. World Labs describes Marble as a world model to distinguish it from reconstruction-only tools.

The technique of extracting 3D geometry from multiple overlapping photographs by identifying common points across images and triangulating their positions in space. It is the foundational step in tools like Luma AI and Polycam, and underlies the stitching stage in Teleport's pipeline before the panorama is handed to World Labs.

A rendering method that projects 3D geometry onto a 2D image in a way that allows gradients to be computed backward through the projection step. This makes it possible to optimize a 3D representation — such as the shape, color, and position of Gaussian ellipsoids — directly from photograph supervision, which is the training mechanism behind 3D Gaussian Splatting.

A Marble 1.1 feature that automatically detects when a captured scene requires more spatial extent than the input panorama implies, and adds up to five additional spatial units in the same generation pass. It addresses the common failure mode where indoor or enclosed spaces need more room than the photography suggests.

A large-scale visual database of over 14 million labeled images across thousands of categories, created by Fei-Fei Li and colleagues starting in 2009. Its annual recognition challenge (ILSVRC) catalyzed the modern deep-learning revolution in computer vision when a neural network dramatically outperformed classical methods in 2012, and remains a foundational benchmark in AI research.

article.fact_check: The tweet claims Teleport is "the only iPhone app that can capture high-quality 360° panoramas." This is a marketing claim that does not survive scrutiny: companion apps for dedicated 360° cameras (Insta360, Ricoh Theta, GoPro MAX) also run on iPhone and capture high-quality panoramas, though they require external hardware. The more defensible claim — which Maly likely intends — is that Teleport is the only app generating full equirectangular panoramas using solely the iPhone's built-in cameras, without auxiliary hardware. Even that narrower claim is difficult to verify without a comprehensive survey of the App Store.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi's 2026 Stock Moves — Motley Fool

ticker_nvda.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ticker_nvda.blurb: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and system-on-chip products. Originally a gaming chip company, it became the dominant supplier of AI accelerators — chips that perform the parallel matrix math required to train and run large language models. Its H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families are the de facto standard for AI training infrastructure at hyperscalers and cloud providers. NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem creates deep switching costs: virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, making competing hardware difficult to adopt at scale. NVIDIA also sells networking (InfiniBand, Ethernet) and data-centre systems.
ticker_nvda.recent: NVIDIA reported FY2026 (ending Jan 2026) revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% YoY, with data centre revenue reaching $186 billion. The company's forward P/E of ~17.5x on 34.8% projected EPS growth produces a PEG of 0.50 — unusually cheap for what is arguably the most critical infrastructure company in the AI buildout. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) collectively committed over $200 billion in AI infrastructure capex for 2026, the majority flowing through NVIDIA's supply chain.

ticker_amd.name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
ticker_amd.blurb: AMD is a fabless semiconductor company that designs CPUs (EPYC for data centres, Ryzen for consumer PCs) and GPUs (Instinct for AI/HPC, Radeon for gaming and workstations). Under CEO Lisa Su, AMD has taken significant data-centre CPU market share from Intel with its EPYC server processors, which now command an estimated 30%+ of the x86 server CPU market. AMD's MI300X and MI350 AI accelerators compete directly with NVIDIA's H100/H200 family and are gaining traction with hyperscalers seeking GPU supply alternatives. All AMD chips are manufactured by TSMC.
ticker_amd.recent: AMD reported strong 2025 revenue growth led by EPYC and Instinct, with data-centre revenue crossing $12 billion annually. Forward P/E of ~32.6x on 63.8% projected EPS growth yields a PEG of 0.51 — compelling for a company with clear data-centre CPU momentum and an AI accelerator portfolio that is gaining customer adoption. NVIDIA's dominant CUDA ecosystem remains the primary competitive barrier for AMD's GPU ambitions.

ticker_adsk.name: Autodesk, Inc.
ticker_adsk.blurb: Autodesk, Inc. provides 3D design, engineering, and entertainment technology solutions worldwide. Its products include AutoCAD, Revit, and Autodesk Build, serving industries such as architecture, engineering, construction, and media. With a market cap of about $51 billion and over 14,000 employees, Autodesk is a leading software company in the design and building information modeling space.
